about_project_desc: This platform was developed as part of a doctoral dissertation for the linguistic analysis of collocation semantics and translation equivalents in English–Uzbek parallel texts.

about_project_text: The platform was developed for the PhD dissertation «A study of collocational words in a parallel corpus of translations and comparable texts (on the material of Uzbek and English)» (Bukhara State University, 10.00.06). Every result is shown with its source: the translation in the book, data extracted automatically from the corpus and reference material are kept apart.
honesty_note: A translation equivalent is always the translator’s own word in the book; AI or machine translation is never shown as an equivalent.
colloc_page_note: This list is a reference base taken from English collocation collections. The Uzbek forms are AI suggestions and are not treated as translation equivalents until the researcher checks them. The real translation equivalents from the books appear on the search page, in the translator’s own words. Statistical measures (MI, t-score, log-likelihood) have not yet been computed against a reference corpus.
dict_hidden_title: The dictionary section is closed for now
dict_hidden_text: The entries taken from the printed dictionaries are full of optical character recognition (OCR) errors: in many cases the word and translation columns are mixed up. Research cannot rely on such data, so the dictionary stays hidden from the public until it is cleaned again. See translation equivalents on the search page, based on the translation in the book.

site_description: Uzbek–English parallel corpus of literary translation: how words and collocations are rendered in the books.
search_intro: Type an Uzbek or English word or collocation. You will see how the translator rendered it, all its forms and derived words, the collocations it forms, and every occurrence next to its parallel sentence in the other book.
home_h1: See how the translator rendered a word, in the book itself
home_lead: TILCOR is an Uzbek–English parallel corpus of works by Cho‘lpon and Hemingway and their translations. Type a word or a collocation: every occurrence stands next to its counterpart in the translation.
home_example_caption: The combination «og‘ir uyqu» and its counterpart in the translation.
home_pair_oms: «The Old Man and the Sea» — «Chol va dengiz»

sec_collocations_note: The candidates are extracted from the corpus: by dependency relations in English, by structural patterns in Uzbek; those occurring at least twice are kept. Each comes with its counterpart in the translation and an example.
coll_none_in_corpus: The corpus has no collocation candidate with this word occurring at least twice.
coll_page_lead: Candidates extracted automatically from the two book pairs and occurring at least twice, with their structural pattern, frequency, counterparts in the translation and examples. Whether a candidate is a collocation is decided by the procedure of section 1.1.4 of the dissertation: the linguistic judgement and the statistical confirmation in a reference corpus.
ref_lists_note: A list taken from English learner collocation collections (Academic Collocation List, English Collocations in Use, 1000 English Collocations). It is not corpus data and is not used in the statistics.
eq_note: An equivalent is the translator’s own words in the book. They were found by word alignment in {with} of {total} sentences; in the rest the translator expressed the idea in another way.
eq_none_found: No word-level counterpart was found for this query: the translator rendered the idea with other words or left it out. The parallel sentences are below.
korpus_lead: The corpus consists of two work–translation pairs. Each work is compared only with its own translation, sentence by sentence.
korpus_pages_text: A page is always the number printed in the copy used: «Kecha va kunduz» — the footer of the ziyouz.com copy; «Night and Day» — the printed page; «The Old Man and the Sea» — the [N] marks in the text; «Chol va dengiz» — the page of the electronic copy, which does not match the 1986 printed edition.
login_lead: This page is for the researcher and the reviewer only. Search and all other sections are open without signing in.

coll_order_note: The association measure is computed within the study corpus; it does not decide the status of a collocation and is given to compare the measures.
coll_assoc_note: O₁₁ is the frequency of the combination; R₁ and C₁ the frequencies of its first and last component in the texts of that language; N the number of tokens of that language. Formulas and the comparison of the measures are on the Statistics page.
coll_eq_found: Occurrences with a counterpart found in the translation: {a} of {b}.
pair_none_translation: Sentence alignment found no counterpart in the translation: the translator left the sentence out, merged it with a neighbouring one, or it was left over in the alignment.
pair_none_original: Sentence alignment found no counterpart in the original: the translator added the sentence, split a sentence of the original, or it was left over in the alignment.

dict_switched_en: This word was found in the English–Uzbek part.
dict_switched_uz: This word was found in the Uzbek–English part.

dict_also_other_uz: The word is also in the Uzbek–English part
dict_method_text: The dictionary is taken neither from a printed dictionary nor from machine translation. It is built automatically from the word alignment of the two books: a translation is included only if it is linked at least three times in the corpus and the two words are associated in both directions. It shows the choices of these two translators, not every meaning the word has in the language.
